body:
On the 27th, National Pension Service (NPS) Chairman Kim Sung-ju said, "If we had not kept the share of domestic stocks in line with reality, the National Pension Service could have fallen into a loss zone."

At a comprehensive audit by the National Assembly Health and Welfare Committee that day, Chairman Kim, responding to questions from Rep. So Byung-hoon of the Democratic Party of Korea about fund management, said, "Right now, domestic stocks are performing the best. Overseas stocks are not doing well, and both domestic and overseas bonds are currently in negative territory," adding that maintaining the share of domestic stocks helped the fund's performance.

He added, "The National Pension Service is a long-term investor," and "If you weigh gains and losses by comparing highs and lows over a few months, a pension fund, as a long-term investor, ends up missing important long-term gains."

To Rep. So's point that there is a misconception that the National Pension Service invests only in domestic stocks, he said, "We invest in more than 80 countries worldwide, and overseas investments account for over 55%." To a question about whether the fund has grown since the start of the year, he answered, "Based on the beginning of this year, it remains high."

Minister Jung Eun-kyeong of the Ministry of Health and Welfare, in response to questions from Rep. Lee Man-hee of the People Power Party about fund management, said, "We share concerns about long-term sustainability and believe there is a need to raise returns."

Asked who should be held accountable for the National Pension Fund Management Committee's decisions, such as deferring domestic stock rebalancing, he said, "Matters decided by the Fund Management Committee are matters the committee must be responsible for." Regarding the government's explanation that the timing of the National Pension Fund's depletion has been pushed back to 2078, he explained the reference point for the estimate by saying, "We reported materials estimated based on last year's year-end returns."

At the comprehensive audit that day, tensions rose between the ruling and opposition parties over disclosing the Fund Management Committee minutes related to the decision to defer domestic stock rebalancing. The People Power Party demanded disclosure, saying the decision process and its impact on the fund must be verified, while the Democratic Party of Korea countered that there was no bipartisan agreement for submitting the materials.

People Power Party Rep. Lee Man-hee demanded that the minutes reveal who led the decision to defer rebalancing. Democratic Party of Korea Rep. Nam In-soon rebutted by citing the legal provision requiring the minutes to be disclosed four years later and the lack of a bipartisan agreement needed for submitting materials to the National Assembly.
